verdict.rationale: Turso documents point-in-time recovery, which restores a database to a specific point in time without a dump, so the "restore to an earlier state" half is covered. Branches are documented as separate database instances, so PITR should apply to them, though no source says so. Re-syncing from the parent is only possible by creating a new branch with `--from-db`, not by resetting an existing one. Missing for 10: an explicit reset-branch-from-parent operation, documentation that PITR works on branch databases, and independent or hands-on corroboration of either workflow.
